backlog.spec: Rewrite compute_max_radii. The current code has a duplicated, mis-indented double loop that overwrites the outer index i and applies a greedy proportional shrink, which is order-dependent and loose. Replace it with an exact solve: for fixed centers, maximize sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i). Use scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) with the sparse constraint matrix. Clip radii at zero and shrink by 1e-9 before returning.
backlog.title: Fix nested-loop bug and compute exact LP radii for fixed centers

backlog.spec: Treat the 26 centers and 26 radii as 78 decision variables and maximize sum(r) with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP'). Constraints: for every pair, (x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0; for every circle, r_i <= x_i, r_i <= y_i, r_i <= 1-x_i, r_i <= 1-y_i. Supply analytic Jacobians for the constraints. Start from a feasible initial configuration (e.g., the LP radii of the initial centers) and run a few SLSQP rounds until the objective change is below 1e-10.
backlog.title: Joint SLSQP over centers and radii

backlog.spec: Use numpy.random.default_rng(seed) with a fixed seed. For K random initial center sets (uniform in the square, with a minimum separation rejection), run a local optimizer to get a valid packing, compute its sum of radii, and keep the best. Choose K so the total run finishes in about 3 minutes, using an iteration budget rather than the wall clock so results stay repeatable.
backlog.title: Multi-start with fixed seed and best-of selection

backlog.spec: Optimize the 78-variable vector (centers and radii) to maximize sum(r) minus mu times the squared violations: sum over pairs of max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 and sum over circles of max(0, r_i - boundary distance)^2. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' and analytic gradients. Increase mu geometrically over stages (for example 10 to 1e6), warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. Finish with the exact LP radii on the final centers.
backlog.title: Penalty method with L-BFGS-B and increasing penalty weight

backlog.spec: Start from a locally optimized packing. Repeat many times: copy the best, perturb the centers of 2 to 4 randomly chosen circles (or relocate the smallest circle to a random point), re-run the local optimizer, and accept the new packing if its sum of radii is higher (Metropolis acceptance with a small temperature is optional). Keep the global best. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: Build a 25-circle optimized packing first. Then find the point in the square that maximizes the distance to all existing centers and to the boundary (sample a dense grid, or use local search from the best grid points). Insert the 26th circle there, and re-optimize all 26 circles jointly with the local optimizer. Return the best of this and the baseline.
backlog.title: Greedy insertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Optimize a packing of 28 to 30 circles with the local optimizer, starting from a jittered hexagonal-like grid. Repeatedly remove the circle with the smallest radius, then re-optimize the remaining set, until exactly 26 circles remain. Re-optimize once more with more iterations. Return the best sum of radii found across the removal path.
backlog.title: Greedy removal from a 30-circle packing

backlog.spec: Stage 1: find the largest common radius r for which 26 equal circles fit, using bisection on r with a feasibility check via a small LP or penalty minimization over centers. Stage 2: use the resulting centers as the starting point, allow radii to vary, and run the joint local optimizer to maximize sum(r). This gives a structured start that avoids the poor local optima of the random start.
backlog.title: Two-stage: equal radii first, then release

backlog.spec: Start with small random radii at random centers. Repeat in steps: grow all radii by a small factor, then resolve overlaps by pushing overlapping pairs apart along their connecting line and clamping radii to the boundary, using a fixed number of relaxation sweeps per step. Shrink the growth factor as the packing becomes jammed. Stop when no growth is possible. Then run the exact LP radii step on the final centers.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style inflation

backlog.spec: Impose a symmetry on the centers, for example mirror symmetry about the diagonal or the 180-degree rotation about the square center, so that only about half the centers are free variables (mirror or rotated copies are generated from them). Optimize the reduced problem with the local optimizer from several random starts. Then release the symmetry and run the full joint optimizer from the best symmetric solution to break ties and gain the last digits.
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained search, then unconstrained polish

backlog.spec: Replace the hard max in the overlap penalty with a softplus of width tau: softplus((r_i+r_j-d_ij)/tau) times tau. Start with a large tau (around 0.05) so gradients flow everywhere, then anneal tau geometrically down to about 1e-5 over stages, re-optimizing with L-BFGS-B at each stage. Finish with the exact LP radii.
backlog.title: Smooth overlap penalty with annealed sharpness

backlog.spec: Implement Adam manually in numpy (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-8) on the energy E = -sum(r) + mu times the squared overlap and boundary violations, with analytic gradients computed by vectorized pairwise numpy broadcasting. Run a fixed number of steps (for example 20000) with a fixed seed, increase mu over time, and keep the iterate with the best feasible (exactly checked) sum of radii.
backlog.title: Hand-coded Adam on the penalty energy

backlog.spec: Within the gradient-based penalty optimizer, use a learning rate that follows cosine annealing from 0.05 down to 1e-5, restarted 4 times with each restart starting from the best configuration found so far (with a small random perturbation of the radii). This helps escape shallow local minima while keeping the best solution. Use a fixed seed and a fixed step count.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate schedule with restarts

backlog.spec: Maximize sum(r) subject to the pairwise and boundary constraints by adding a log barrier -mu * sum(log(slack)) for each constraint slack, where slack = d_ij^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 or the boundary slacks. Minimize with Newton or L-BFGS-B, and decrease mu by a factor of 10 over about 8 stages. The iterates stay strictly feasible throughout, so no final repair is needed beyond a tiny shrink.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior point on constraints

backlog.spec: After any optimization, compute every pairwise and boundary constraint exactly in double precision. If any violation exists, fix it with the exact LP radii on the centers (which is always feasible), clip centers into [0,1] first, and then multiply all radii by (1 - 1e-9). Assert feasibility before returning so the harness never sees an overlap. This wraps all other ideas as a safety layer.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility repair and safety shrink

backlog.spec: Optimize the joint problem with a weighted objective, maximize sum(w_i * r_i) with random positive weights w_i drawn from a fixed seed (for example uniform in [0.8, 1.2]). The weighting drives the search toward different radius-size distributions and out of symmetric local optima. Then run the unweighted joint optimizer from the best weighted solution. Keep the best result by unweighted sum.
backlog.title: Weighted objective to break symmetry

backlog.spec: Inside the iterative local optimizer, add Gaussian noise to the centers at each outer step, with standard deviation that decays geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-4 over the run. Each step re-solves the exact LP radii for the noisy centers and accepts the new packing only if its sum is higher. This acts as a regularizer that lets large-scale rearrangements happen early and fine tuning happen late.
backlog.title: Annealed coordinate noise during optimization

backlog.spec: Rewrite all overlap, gradient, and distance calculations with numpy broadcasting over the full 26x26 pair matrix using precomputed index masks for the upper triangle, with no Python loops over pairs. This speeds each local optimization several-fold so that many more random restarts fit inside the time budget. Keep the same objective and produce identical results to the loop version for a given input.
backlog.title: Vectorized pairwise computation for fast restarts

backlog.spec: Store a batch of B candidate packings (for example B=32) as a single array of shape (B, 26, 3) for (x, y, r). Run gradient-based penalty descent on all candidates simultaneously using vectorized numpy operations over the batch axis. Periodically keep the top half by exact sum of radii and replace the bottom half with perturbed copies of the top half. Return the best candidate after a fixed number of generations.
backlog.title: Batched parallel local optimization of many starts

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of about 20 valid packings. Create children by crossover: take the circles on one side of a random line through the square from parent A and the rest from parent B, fix the circle count to 26 by removing or adding random circles, then run the local optimizer on the child. Replace the worst population member when the child is better. Use a fixed seed and an iteration budget.
backlog.title: Genetic crossover of packings

backlog.spec: Initialize with a deliberate size gradient: place a few large circles near the center and progressively smaller circles toward the four edges and corners, with the 26 positions chosen on a jittered grid whose local density matches those sizes. Use the LP radii as the starting radii, then run the joint optimizer. This targets arrangements where big circles sit in the middle and small ones fill the border gaps.
backlog.title: Mixed-size structured start: large center, small border

backlog.spec: Generate a hexagonal lattice of points with spacing chosen so that about 26 points fall inside the unit square, using alternate rows offset by half a spacing. Keep exactly 26 points (adding or dropping boundary points as needed), add small random jitter from a fixed seed, and use these as centers. Compute the LP radii and run the joint local optimizer. This explores whether a lattice-based basin improves on the hand-placed rings.
backlog.title: Jittered hexagonal lattice start with edge truncation

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii for the 26 circles from a log-uniform distribution between 0.02 and 0.15 with a fixed seed, and draw centers uniformly in the square. Immediately compute the exact LP radii for these centers to get a feasible start, then optimize jointly. Run this with several seeds inside the time budget and keep the best. The varied initial sizes encourage diverse basins.
backlog.title: Random log-uniform radius initialization

backlog.spec: Start from a 5 by 5 grid of centers (25 points) with spacing that fills the square, add one extra center in a random interior location, and jitter all points slightly with a fixed seed. Compute exact LP radii and optimize the full joint problem. Also try the variant where the grid is 4 by 4 plus 10 interior points. Return the best result.
backlog.title: Square-grid start with one extra circle

backlog.spec: On a current good packing, try discrete moves: pick a small circle and move it to a random point in the square (or into the largest empty region), then re-optimize with the local optimizer. Accept only improvements in exact sum of radii. Repeat for a fixed number of moves. This is a discrete complement to continuous optimization and escapes configurations where a single misplaced small circle wastes space.
backlog.title: Iterative pair-swap and relocation local search

backlog.spec: Rescale the optimization variables so that centers and radii have comparable magnitudes, for example optimize over s = x/0.1 for centers and q = r/0.1 for radii, and map back before evaluating constraints. Use the same local optimizer and keep the scaling consistent across gradient and constraint evaluation. Better conditioning reduces the number of iterations and avoids early termination from tiny gradients on small radii.
backlog.title: Preconditioned variable scaling

backlog.spec: Structure the whole optimization as a sequence of stages with a fixed iteration cap per stage (not a wall clock, to keep results deterministic). After every stage, compute the exact feasible sum of radii of the current configuration (via the LP radii step) and store the best feasible packing seen. Stop when the improvement over the last three stages is below 1e-9 or the global cap is reached. Return the best stored packing, shrunk by a tiny margin.
backlog.title: Iteration budget control with best-so-far tracking

incumbent.description: Adds a batched stage (B=32 candidates stored as a (B,26,2) array) that runs vectorized penalty descent at a fixed target radius, scores each candidate by exact LP sum of radii, and keeps the top half while replacing the bottom half with perturbed copies, before the existing annealing and SLSQP stages.
